subset_files: Place BATADAL challenge CSV files locally under data/raw/batadal/.
selected_faults: Native attack labels from the challenge files.
selection_rationale: Water-distribution attacks are a strong water/process-control analog when source provenance is defensible.
limitation: Do not report BATADAL results unless the raw source and label semantics are documented.

subset_files: Use official local DAMADICS CSV/MAT files if available under data/raw/damadics/.
selected_faults: Fault-free, natural faulty, and artificial faulty states where labels are available.
selection_rationale: Industrial actuator benchmark strengthens the actuation/process-control angle.
limitation: Not included in quantitative tables unless official raw files are locally present and parsed.

subset_files: Use one fixed train CSV/GZ and one fixed test CSV/GZ from the same HAI version.
selected_faults: Native HAI attack/anomaly labels in the selected test file.
selection_rationale: Public ICS benchmark gives closed-loop process context while keeping analysis tractable.
limitation: HAI cyber-physical attacks are not identical to hydroponic sensor faults.

subset_files: Use the UCI CSV and prepare the first 100000 rows unless a labeled event-window file is added locally.
selected_faults: Native maintenance/failure events only when defensibly sourced; otherwise synthetic sensor faults.
selection_rationale: Adds a real industrial multivariate sensor dataset without very large process-control archives.
limitation: MetroPT-3 is predictive-maintenance data and does not directly encode hydroponic actuation safety.

subset_files: Use all CSV files under the SKAB data directory, including anomaly-free calibration and labeled anomaly experiments.
selected_faults: Native SKAB anomaly/changepoint labels from valve and other process-loop experiments.
selection_rationale: A compact, fully public, labeled process-loop benchmark strengthens external validation without oversized downloads.
limitation: SKAB faults are process-loop anomalies, not hydroponic-specific sensor faults or agronomic outcomes.

subset_files: Use approved local normal/test CSV files if available under data/raw/swat/.
selected_faults: Native normal/attack labels from approved SWaT files.
selection_rationale: Request-access water-treatment benchmark tests transfer to sensor/actuator water processes.
limitation: Not included in quantitative tables unless approved raw files are locally present.

subset_files: Use a small converted TEP CSV/XLSX source placed under data/raw/tep/; do not require the 133 GB DTU archive.
selected_faults: fault-free plus five representative process faults covering abrupt, drift-like, disturbance, noise-like, and slow/hard-to-detect behavior.
selection_rationale: Predefined fault-diversity subset evaluates cross-domain robustness without claiming exhaustive TEP dominance.
limitation: Subset results support plausibility and robustness only; full-archive TEP benchmarking is optional.

subset_files: Use fault-free plus representative fault CSV/XLSX runs placed under data/raw/tep_csv/.
selected_faults: faultNumber != 0, preferably abrupt, drift-like, disturbance, noise-like, and slow/hard-to-detect cases.
selection_rationale: Keeps TEP validation tractable while preserving chemical-process relevance.
limitation: Subset TEP CSV results support robustness claims only; they are not exhaustive TEP benchmarking.

subset_files: Use approved local normal/test CSV files if available under data/raw/wadi/.
selected_faults: Native normal/attack labels from approved WaDi files.
selection_rationale: Distributed water-process benchmark tests scalability beyond the hydroponic target system.
limitation: Not included in quantitative tables unless approved raw files are locally present.

subset_files: Use only extracted greenhouse climate/control time-series files placed under data/raw/wur/.
selected_faults: No native anomaly labels assumed; use normal greenhouse periods plus synthetic spike, drift, dropout, bias, noise-burst, and step faults.
selection_rationale: Domain-adjacent CEA validation tests false alarms and synthetic-fault behavior without downloading image-heavy archives.
limitation: WUR subset does not support supervised anomaly claims unless defensible event labels are present locally.
